critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
C18, evidence_table at 75c2212. The page camera is now a usable compositing plate. The stage as a whole is not at pro level, because only page was re-rendered.

The page plate: all three P1s from r5 are fixed, and I measured each one.

(1) Cushion shading is gone.
- On the raw frame, luma 3 mm inside each edge is 0.98 to 1.01 of luma 20 mm inside. Head averages 0.993, right 0.985, foot 0.994, left 1.008.
- The paper has no dark rim, and all four corners are sharp points.
- At most there is a faint contact line on the wood, about 1 mm wide, along the middle and lower parts of the far right edge: raw 44-48 at 0.3-0.6 mm out, against 50-51 from 1.5 mm out. Along the upper third of that edge the wood reads 37-39 right up to the paper, with no shadow.

(2) The bulb glint is gone.
- The wood around the pen grades about 30 (median 29) and is matt.
- The brightest area in frame outside the paper is now the highlighter itself (80 px block mean, raw 118-119). Wood p99 grades about 65.

(3) The paper is warm again.
- Graded centre is 184.8/181.1/178.0. The sheet averages R-B +8.4 and G-B +3.8.
- Graded luma on the sheet runs 142 to 184 (p1 to p99): a gentle falloff from left of centre toward the head-right corner.
- Paper texture is essentially nil (raw high-pass std about 0.4-0.5), which is right for a plate.

The geometry is good:
- The text angle on screen is now 14-17 degrees.
- Margins are 10% at the top and 8% at the bottom.
- The paper-to-wood contrast is at least 2.5:1 on every side. Medians run from 2.9:1 on the lit left edge to 3.7:1 at the head, and the lowest values are on the lower half of the left edge.

What still keeps the page frame below fern:
- The highlighter grades as a pastel khaki tube: the body is about 138/129/97 (hue about 47 degrees, saturation mostly 0.21-0.28) under a darker olive cap. It reads as a glue stick, not a fluorescent marker. It is chunky and toy-like, with no chisel tip and no clip, and it is the second brightest object in frame.
- The wood still reads as procedural:
  - The grain is one repeating sinuous band.
  - Pale scratch streaks remain around the sheet's foot: near-vertical ones below its lower-left corner, and diagonal ones below the foot and to the right of the foot-right corner.
  - The board end-joint at the top left, with its rounded, light-catching bevels, reads as laminate decking. A second end-joint grazes the right frame edge.
- The pen, sheet and highlighter make a symmetric stock-mockup layout. On screen, the pen, both long edges of the sheet and the marker all run within about 8 degrees of each other.
- No depth-of-field data ships with the pins. The head edge measures 2.5-2.9 px (10-90%), against 1.5-1.9 px at the foot.

The rest of the stage has not moved since r5:
- pair.jpg is still the render published at 07:54 in 6b5702c, before d25cd94. Both sheets still have cushioned, dark-rimmed edges and dark rounded foot-right corners, the pen still lies across the left sheet's edge, and the lamp-base arc still shows at the top left.
- screen.jpg is still 1280x720.
- overhead, push, laptop, purses and passport are the round-4 renders of 7249565, regraded to A fixed at 06:14.
  - Overhead has 27.8% of graded pixels with luma below 8 (17% below 8 in all three channels). Straight vertical tone steps cut rectangular patches into the dark wood.
  - Purses still has the ring crescent and the haze bank on the burgundy bag.
- Against the koi-pond stills' surface craft, the wood and paper here are still flat CG.

One good plate does not lift a stage whose other seven frames are stale. Two of those are broken plates (pair and screen).
answers:
1. Score evidence_table at 75c2212: see the scores. This commit changed only page.jpg, page.png and page.corners.json. Pair and screen are the 07:54 renders of 6b5702c. The five story cameras are the round-4 renders of 7249565, regraded at 06:14. I scored what is published, not the code.

2. Tracking: I verified the single-page pins independently.

Method:
- Sampled 120 luma profiles across each edge of the raw page.png, bilinear at 0.1 px steps.
- Took the half-maximum crossing between paper (20-40 px inside) and wood (20-40 px outside).
- Fitted a line to each edge (residual RMS 0.07-0.10 px, max 0.30 px) and intersected neighbouring lines.

Visible corners against the JSON pins (top-left pixel-edge origin):

| Corner | Visible corner (px) | JSON pin (px) | Distance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top left | 1088.01, 149.36 | 1088.515, 150.501 | 1.25 px |
| Top right | 1815.06, 336.40 | 1814.544, 336.860 | 0.69 px |
| Bottom right | 1512.00, 1320.14 | 1512.010, 1319.701 | 0.44 px |
| Bottom left | 676.97, 1065.37 | 677.293, 1065.108 | 0.42 px |

- Your "within 1.27 px" holds. The worst corner is 1.25 px off, at the top left.
- Every visible edge sits outside the pinned quad: by 0.78 px at the head, 0.24 px on the right, 0.39 px at the foot and 0.56 px on the left.
- A page pinned exactly to the JSON will leave a sliver of blank paper, up to about 1 px wide. It is worst along the head, where the blank paper is brightest against the wood. Dilate the pinned page by 1 px, or pin to the corners above (fix 4).
- It is a still, so tracking means a static pin. Any 2D push added in post must apply the same transform to the pins.

3. Graded centre RGB 185/181/178: confirmed. I measure 184.8/181.1/178.0 over 10x10 px at the homography centre (1280, 679).
- Raw there is 202/184/161.
- The warmth survives the grade: R-B is +7 at the centre and +8.4 over the sheet. That is slightly warm, as the brief asks.
- The peak is about 184 (72% of white). That is dim for a fern document insert, but right for this noir grade.

4. 3 mm edge samples within 1.5% of the 20 mm samples: true on average, not at every sample.

On the raw frame (9 stations per edge, ratio of 3 mm to 20 mm):

| Edge | Range | Mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Head | 0.985-0.998 | 0.993 |
| Right | 0.981-0.988 | 0.985 |
| Foot | 0.990-0.998 | 0.994 |
| Left | 1.001-1.012 | 1.008 |

- The worst single sample is about 2% darker, on the right edge. That is well inside the 5% target, so I pass it.
- At 1 mm the worst sample is about 0.98. At 0.5 mm it is about 0.96. The 0.5 mm sample is 1.7 px from the edge and inside the edge's own defocus.
- On the graded frame the 3 mm/20 mm ratio is 0.954-0.992. That drop comes from the vignette and the lamp falloff, and it belongs in the comp.

5. The r5 P1s:

- Cushion shading: fixed.
  - document_plates() now sets use_smooth = False on each sheet.
  - plate_paper has no edge_tone.
  - There is no dark rim and no rounded corner.
  - On the wood there is at most a faint contact line, about 1 mm wide, along the middle and lower parts of the far right edge: raw 44-48 at 0.3-0.6 mm out, against 50-51 from 1.5 mm out. There is none on the upper third.
- Bulb glint by the pen: fixed.
  - For beat 'plate', visible_glossy is off on lamp_spot, lamp_glow and lamp_bulb, the lights' specular_factor is 0, and the table uses plate_wood at roughness 0.63.
  - The wood by the pen grades about 30.
  - Beside the lit left edge, the wood reads raw 61-72 against paper at 192-198, about 2.7-3.2:1. The lowest single station is 2.55:1.
- Grade turning the paper neutral: fixed. The centre grades R-B +7, G-B +3.

The lamp-base arc is also gone from page. The sheet turn is now -18 degrees, so text runs at 14-17 degrees on screen.

6. Still open on page:
- The highlighter reads khaki.
  - Graded body: about 138/129/97 (luma median 136), peak about 164/158/136, hue about 47 degrees, saturation mostly 0.21-0.28.
  - The cap is a darker olive, about 104/98/59, at saturation about 0.47.
- The wood has its scratches, its end-joints and its repeating grain.
- The corners JSON carries no focus or depth data. The head edge is 2.5-2.9 px (10-90%), against 1.5-1.9 px at the foot, so a pinned page needs about 1 px more blur at the head.
- The top-right frame corner is under video black.
  - It grades about 7/6/7 over an 80 px patch, and about 5/3/4 in its last 10 px.
  - The cause is the approved vignette over raw wood of about 21/12/5.
  - 0.23% of the frame's pixels are below 8 in all three channels.
- page_foot exists in code but has not been published: loc (0.03, -0.306, TOP+0.346), f/8.

7. Pair, screen and page_foot (still rendering):
- Nothing new is published for pair, so it still fails on the old build:
  - cushioned sheet edges
  - dark rounded foot-right corners
  - the pen across the left sheet's edge
  - the lamp-base arc
- The code at HEAD addresses all four. It places the pen at (-0.21, 0.02, 80), clear of document_left's left edge at x of about -0.169. Re-measure the pair the same way once it lands.
- screen.png is still 1280x720, though CAMERAS['screen'] now asks for 2560.

fixes.problem:
The published pair plate (6b5702c, 07:54, before d25cd94) still has the old sheet build:
- Both sheets darken over their last 12-15 mm on the right and foot edges. On the raw, the 3 mm/20 mm ratio there is 0.18-0.64.
- The foot-right corners are dark and rounded.
- The pen lies across the left sheet's left edge.
- The lamp-base double arc shows at the top left.
- 2.3% of graded pixels have luma below 8 (0.9% in all three channels).
As published, it cannot carry a pinned page.
fixes.fix:
Publish the pair render from HEAD at 2560x1440 with a fresh pair.corners.json. HEAD already has:
- use_smooth=False on the sheets
- plate_paper without edge_tone
- the lamp meshes hidden from camera for beat 'plate'
- the pen at (-0.21, 0.02, 80)

Then run the same checks as page:
- Luma 3 mm inside each edge of both sheets within 3% of luma 20 mm inside.
- No prop inside either pinned quad.
- Each visible corner within 1.5 px of its pin.
- Graded sheet centres at R-B +6 to +10.

fixes.problem:
The document_highlighter reads as a pastel khaki glue stick, not a fluorescent marker:
- Graded body about 138/129/97, peak about 164/158/136, hue about 47 degrees, saturation mostly 0.21-0.28.
- The cap is a darker olive (about 104/98/59).
- The 'yellow document marker' plastic (0.80, 0.60, 0.035) renders raw at about 181/151/66, and grade A's saturation 0.55 leaves it pale.
- pp.highlighter is a 16 mm oval tube with a rounded tail, no chisel tip and no clip, so it reads as a toy.
- It is the brightest object in frame outside the paper, and it pulls the eye off the sheet.
fixes.fix:
Either drop it from the page camera (show=('page sheet', 'document tools')), or rebuild it as a real highlighter.

To rebuild:
1. Material: base about (0.95, 0.86, 0.02), roughness 0.6.
   - The saturation has to come from the albedo, because grade A cuts saturation whatever lights the surface.
   - The cap (raw about 144/120/21) already grades at about 0.47; the body (raw about 181/151/66) grades at about 0.28.
   - A weak emission of the same colour (strength 0.2-0.3) can stand in for fluorescence if the body still reads dull. Do not change the grade.
2. Geometry, in a page-only builder (do not change pp.highlighter for other cameras):
   - Reduce r from 0.0082 to about 0.0062.
   - Replace the rounded tail with a flat end cap.
   - Add a 2 mm x 30 mm clip on the cap. Alternatively, lay it uncapped, with a 5-6 mm chisel nib showing and the cap beside it.
3. Target on the graded frame:
   - body hue 52-58 degrees
   - saturation at least 0.45
   - peak luma no higher than about 0.8 of the paper beside it

fixes.problem:
The plate_wood still reads as procedural:
- One repeating sinuous grain band runs across every board.
- Pale scratch streaks remain around the sheet's foot (coordinates at 2560):
  - near-vertical ones below its lower-left corner (about x 860-940, y 1110-1210)
  - diagonal ones below the foot (about x 1150-1320, y 1260-1390)
  - diagonal ones to the right of the foot-right corner (about x 1600-1800, y 1000-1220)
  - finer diagonals to the right of the highlighter
- The board end-joint at the top left (x about 430-510, y 0-680) has rounded, light-catching bevels and reads as laminate decking. A second end-joint grazes the right frame edge (x about 2530-2555, y 690-900).
- A broad dark grain sweep along the bottom edge (x 1450-2100, y 1340-1440) reads like the shadow of an off-frame object.
fixes.fix:
1. In materials(), change plate_wood's scratches from 0.5 to 0.15.
2. For the plate wood only (a plate-only variant of worn_wood, or a new argument):
   - Cut the ring-band contrast (late x 0.55) by about 30%.
   - Strengthen the existing pore streaks (pores at mapping (18, 900, 900), pore_m 0.62-0.72), which do not read at about 3.5 px/mm.
   The aim is grain that reads as oak or walnut, not painted waves.
3. The end-joints are table geometry, not the material. table() cuts board 2 (y 0 to 0.26) at x = -0.17, which is the top-left joint, and board 1 (y -0.26 to 0) at x = 0.37, which grazes the right edge.
   - Shifting the document set and cameras by +0.05 m in x would move the top-left joint only about 175 px left, to about x 300, and would bring board 1's joint further into frame.
   - Move board 2's joint to about x = -0.60. The page frame's left edge on that board is at about x = -0.32.
   - If wanted, also move board 1's joint to about 0.45 or beyond.
   - Then check the other cameras that see those boards.
4. Check on the graded frame: no single scratch line longer than 60 px within 300 px of the sheet, and no board end-joint in frame.

fixes.problem:
The JSON pins are the top-face vertices. The visible half-maximum paper edge sits 0.24-0.78 px outside the pinned quad on every side, 0.78 px at the head, so a page pinned exactly will leave a thin sliver of blank paper.

No defocus data ships either. The head edge measures 2.5-2.9 px (10-90%) and the foot 1.5-1.9 px, so a uniformly sharp pinned page will look pasted on at the head.
fixes.fix:
In frame_metadata(), for page, page_foot and pair:
- Add top-level 'focus_m' (camera to its focus empty), 'fstop', 'lens_mm' and 'sensor_mm'.
- Add a 'depth_m' for each corner.

Also write a paper matte next to page.png:
- Set pass_index=1 on document_single.
- Enable view_layer.use_pass_object_index.
- Save an 8-bit page.mask.png through an ID Mask node with anti-aliasing on.
The comp can then clip the pinned page to the real silhouette instead of the quad.

As a check, the half-maximum edge-line fit should be within 0.3 px of the pins; otherwise the comp dilates the page by 1 px.

fixes.problem: The foot-of-page camera exists in code but is not published, so the lower-half insert still has no plate. In code it is CAMERAS['page_foot']: loc (0.03, -0.306, TOP+0.346), aim (0.03, -0.105, TOP), f/8, focus empty fx_page_foot.
fixes.fix:
Render page_foot at 2560x1440 and publish it with page_foot.corners.json. The head corners will be off-frame. Flag each corner with an 'in_frame' boolean, so the comp knows which ones are extrapolated.

Check:
- Both foot corners are at least 8% above the bottom edge and at least 5% from the sides.
- Graded paper R-B is +6 to +10.
- The 3 mm/20 mm edge ratio is at least 0.97 on the raw frame.
- No scratch or end-joint is in frame.

fixes.problem:
screen.png is still 1280x720 (6b5702c, 07:54), though CAMERAS['screen'] has final_res=(2560, 1440) and frame_metadata now lists 'screen'. The plate has no corners file.

In the published frame:

fixes.fix:
1. Re-render screen from HEAD at 2560 and publish screen.corners.json.
2. The key caps ('blank laptop caps') are already near-black: albedo 0.035-0.040, roughness 0.54. What lights them is the screen, most likely the panel's own reflection in the caps.

fixes.fix:
1. Re-render overhead, push, laptop, purses and passport from HEAD at 1280x720, then regrade with A fixed. The bounce, passport and purses changes from 6d658fb are not in these frames yet.
2. Check the re-render for the vertical steps first. worn_wood's per-board tone varies only between boards (along y), so it cannot make a step that crosses every board. If the steps remain, find which light, volume or render-region edge lands at world x of about -0.34 and 0.19 before changing the wood.

fixes.problem:
The pen, sheet and highlighter flank each other symmetrically, a stock-mockup layout with no sense of a working table. On screen, the pen (world turn 80), both long edges of the sheet and the marker (turn 72) all run within about 8 degrees of each other, and nothing in the shot moves.

The top-right frame corner falls under video black: about 7/6/7 over an 80 px patch and 5/3/4 in its last 10 px. That is the approved vignette over raw wood of about 21/12/5.
fixes.fix:
1. Turn the pen well off the sheet's edge direction. For example, centre it at (-0.17, -0.08) and turn it about 30 degrees. That keeps it about 30 mm off the paper and about 100 px inside the frame's left edge.
2. If the marker stays, keep it on the wood to the right of the sheet, at a different angle from the pen. For example, centre it at (0.22, -0.04) and turn it about 115 degrees, about 80 px clear of the right edge in frame. Do not use (0.17, 0.05): that point is inside the sheet's outline.
3. Optional: lift the far-right corner with a plate-only fill on the wood, not with exposure. Moving exposure from -1.18 to -1.10 adds only about 6%, which is far from enough there and would brighten the paper as well. Do not change the grade.
4. Plan the shot's movement as a 2D push in comp of at most 4% over the hold, and apply the same transform to the pins.
